Summary: A study in Scotland found that using a fallowing system resulted in lower lice numbers on Atlantic salmon in cages [1026]. Another study in Australia, however, found no difference in mortality from Amoebic Gill Disease in cages where a fallowing system was used [1026]. A replicated, controlled study in Norway discovered that salmon bred for high resistance to infectious pancreatic necrosis had higher survival rates when exposed to the disease compared to a family bred for low resistance [735].
Statements: ['A study in Scotland found that using a fallowing system resulted in lower lice numbers on Atlantic salmon in cages.', 'A study in Australia found no difference in mortality from Amoebic Gill Disease in cages where a fallowing system was used.', 'A replicated, controlled study in Norway discovered that salmon bred for high resistance to infectious pancreatic necrosis had higher survival rates when exposed to the disease compared to a family bred for low resistance.']

Summary: Two controlled studies in Iceland and Norway found that vaccinated salmon had higher survival rates after being exposed to certain disease-causing bacteria [733]. Additionally, two controlled studies in Australia and Canada reported higher survival in salmon infected with marine flexibacteriosis and bacterial kidney disease after vaccination [733]. For salmon vaccinated against infectious salmon anaemia, two controlled studies in Norway yielded similar results [733]. On the other hand, a replicated study in Australia showed that salmon housed in larger cages had reduced levels of amoebic gill disease when compared to those in smaller cages [742].
Statements: ['Vaccinated salmon had higher survival rates after being exposed to certain disease-causing bacteria.', 'Salmon infected with marine flexibacteriosis and bacterial kidney disease had higher survival rates after vaccination.', 'Salmon vaccinated against infectious salmon anaemia had higher survival rates.', 'Salmon housed in larger cages had reduced levels of amoebic gill disease when compared to salmon in smaller cages.']
